resale_co.name: Resale Certificate of Occupancy (continuing Certificate of Occupancy)
requirements: Completed resale application and fee, with the buyer's contact information
Original sealed survey and elevation certificate dated within 1 year of the resale date
Current-year smoke and CO alarm certificate from the Ocean County Fire Marshal
Recorded Declaration of Deed Restriction (flood regulations covenant)
Work done without required permits will be cited; any open permits must be closed before the CO is issued
Water heater relief valve piped to within 6 inches of the floor
Enclosed spaces below the base flood elevation must comply
Proper fire separation between the garage and living area
Double-keyed deadbolts replaced with an inside thumb turn
Handrail on stairs with 4 or more risers; guards on walking surfaces 30 inches or more above grade
Public Works check of the curb box, meter pit and sewer clean-out
House numbers at least 4 inches tall, contrasting with the background
Driveway no wider than 18 feet at the pavement edge; trash corral and landscaping at least 5 feet from the pavement
Right-of-way cleared of obstructions except mailboxes; easements and corner sight triangles kept clear
Fences on the Boulevard set back 2 feet with a flat walkable surface

resale_co.how_to_apply: Print the Resale CO Application and the Resale CO Checklist from the Zoning Office page, complete them (seller, buyer, agent, sale price, property type) and drop them off with the fee at Borough Hall, 7606 Long Beach Blvd, Harvey Cedars. Include the sealed survey and elevation certificate, the Ocean County Fire Marshal smoke/CO certificate and the recorded Declaration of Deed Restriction. If a deficiency is found, the Zoning Officer contacts the applicant or agent. If the property will be demolished and not occupied, a letter from the buyer and the application are all that is required.

resale_co.notes: Harvey Cedars requires a new Certificate of Occupancy on every sale or transfer of ownership (Chapter 13 Zoning, Transfer of Ownership; the Borough posts an April 2026 print of the chapter). The fee is $50 per living unit on both the Zoning Office page and the 2026 ordinance text. The checklist is dated 12/29/2022 and the application file is labeled 2025. No lead time or validity period is published. The Borough code (12-2.15, January 2021 code book) says no certificate of occupancy will be issued until taxes, assessments, and water and sewer charges are paid; a temporary 30 day CO can be issued on a transfer if they are paid within 30 days. The application form prints the phone as 609-361-6000 x 106; the Zoning Office page gives option 8. Office hours are 9 to 11 am Wednesday and Friday. The Zoning Office says a professional home inspection is recommended; the Borough inspection is visual only.

requirements: Smoke alarms, including hardwired ones, must be under 10 years old (Ocean County Fire Marshal, February 2025)
Battery-only and plug-in CO alarms should be under 5 years old; combination smoke/CO alarms under 10 years old
Homes built before 1978: at least one 10-year sealed battery smoke alarm on each level; newer homes need hardwired alarms by build year, and hardwired alarms must stay hardwired
Wall-mounted alarms 4 to 12 inches from the ceiling, 4 inches from corners and 3 feet from air registers
Homes with a generator, solar or battery system need a printed (not handwritten) 'CAUTION: MULTIPLE SOURCES OF POWER' label within 18 inches of the main panel and the meter
A monitored low-voltage fire alarm system needs a copy of its NFPA 72 test report sent to the office before closing
Borough resale checklist requires a fire certificate for the current year

authorities.how_to_apply: Fill out the Ocean County Fire Marshal's online application (SeamlessDocs). The office then calls to schedule the inspection. Do not mail payment: pay at the inspection by paper check payable to Ocean County Fire Marshal (OCFM), credit card or e-check. No cash. Inspections are done from the Manahawkin office, 179 South Main St.

fire_cert.notes: The Ocean County Fire Marshal is Harvey Cedars' fire code enforcing agency (registry code C) and its Resale & Rental page lists Harvey Cedars for resales and rentals of 1-2 family buildings. The state directory lists Harvey Cedars under directory code 1509 (Watchdog code 1510) with Fire Official Dennis Allen, (732) 370-7360, dallen@co.ocean.nj.us; the Fire Marshal's own page gives (732) 929-2088 and OCFMSmokeDetect@co.ocean.nj.us for residential smoke inspections. The certificate is valid 12 months. The Fire Marshal's page still uses the name CSACMAPFEC and says fees took effect January 1, 2019; the February 2025 requirements sheet says portable fire extinguishers are no longer required. The fee sheet also warns of a minimum $1000.00 fine for closing without the certificate. Contact email for Bree Dominguez is bdominguez@co.ocean.nj.us (Fire Marshal staff page).
